## Acceptance Criteria

*Format: GIVEN / WHEN / THEN, one or more per core rule and per formula, then cross-system and budget criteria. Tags: **(auto)** an automated unit or integration test on the pure resolver (FT-39) or the poll logic that runs **headless** in the mandated CI command (`tests/unit/failure_and_trail/`, `tests/integration/failure_and_trail/`), BLOCKING; **(auto-render)** an automated test that needs rendered pixels (captures, bit-identity, dither, containment) and runs on the named render job `ft-render` (FT-40), never on the headless job, BLOCKING; **(lint)** a static or build-time scan, BLOCKING; **(manual)** a retained capture in `production/qa/evidence/` with sign-off by the named lead, BLOCKING (Visual/Feel and UI evidence is not waived at `qa.level: minimal`); **(spike)** needs a measured spike, named by id, with its pass threshold stated, before the story can close. Fixtures are the data files of `tests/fixtures/failure_and_trail/` (FT-40: `FX-CRYO`, `FX-SEAM`, `FX-TELL`, `fx_row_oracle.json` and the three budget fixtures). Performance criteria are gated on the two reference machines of `project.yaml` `qa.min_spec` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*: **RM-DESKTOP** (Windows 10/11 64-bit; 6-core / 6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class; 8 GB RAM; GPU of the GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / Radeon RX 570 4 GB class, Vulkan 1.2+; SATA SSD; 1920x1080 at 60 Hz; P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 16.6 ms) and **RM-DECK** (Steam Deck LCD 2022, SteamOS stable, 1280x800 at 60 Hz, 30 fps target, ceiling 33.3 ms). Every wall-clock figure is a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release export template, not the editor and not a debug template), renderer `forward_plus`, vsync on, 120 warm-up frames, with the startup read-back (renderer, driver) recorded; a frame-level pass needs P99 <= 90 % of the ceiling (headroom >= 1.7 ms desktop, >= 3.3 ms Deck); the developer's machine is indicative only. A criterion that names RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK passes only when it passes on each; a value not yet measured is "pending spike measurement on RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK", not blocked. **Measurement protocol for every frame-time criterion** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the criterion states its sample (at least 600 Graph steps, about 3,600 render frames, of a scripted player walking at `V_WALK`, and at least 100 samples in every frame class it judges), its percentile method (nearest-rank p99 over the samples of that class) and writes a **host header** into its evidence file (CPU, GPU, OS, driver, display mode and whether the run was an editor or an exported run, as recorded by the harness). The header records what ran and is checked against the named machines and build above. **Reviewer pool RP-3 (defined once, cited by every reviewing criterion):** three reviewers, none of whom authored the capture and none of whom has seen its label: the art-director, the qa-lead and one participant from outside the team (a PT-1 participant); each classifies independently and in writing before any discussion; unless a criterion states another threshold, a classification passes when all three are correct for m and l at `k_auto` and the first zoom-out, and at least two of three are correct for s-tier captures and for k = 1. Citation form `[FT-n; LS-n; PR-n; CR-n; SL-n; EM-n; pillar]`: `LS-` the Life-Support Graph, `PR-` the Pipeline, `CR-` the kernel, `SL-` Save/Load, `EM-` Emitter State; `D.n` a formula of this GDD. Captures are taken **lit** (the chest lamp's beam on the trail) unless a criterion says dark. Every number is a registry constant, a Graph value cited by name, a worked value from this GDD's formulas, or a **[PLACEHOLDER]** default; every pass or fail value is stated in the criterion, never only behind a citation. Criteria that need the GA-T fields (`mode_steps`, `grow_steps`) set them in the fixture feed, so they run now against the resolver; the Graph-side half of GA-T is checked by the Graph's own criteria. Criterion ids are stable handles in one sequence (AC-1 to AC-188, with lettered splits); groups are by topic, so ids within a group are not contiguous. Criteria that wait on a neighbour that does not exist yet (the VS-B MIRROR path), and the points that are not testable as written, are in **Gaps / untestable as written** at the end. A *drawing row* means a row of the table of record (Detailed Design section 6) that draws at the descriptor's current `sev`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the (auto-render) tag, the runner, the fixture root, the reviewer pool and the reference machine are new.)*

### A. Identity, statelessness and the truth channel

- **AC-1 Rebuild equivalence.** GIVEN a scripted run to Graph step N with 17 live and dead descriptors, WHEN the derived render state (stamp set, `size_idx`, extents, `dull_step`, `density_level`, frame indices at a fixed `present_time`) is dumped, the trail scene is torn down, and the scene is rebuilt from one `ALL` plus `present_time`, THEN the two dumps are equal field for field. (auto) [FT-1, FT-16; LS-20; P1]
- **AC-2 No state, no block, no hook.** GIVEN the source and scene tree, WHEN a static scan runs, THEN it finds no registered `block_id`, step hook or command, no light node, no `true_value()` call, no `Tween`, timer node, fade state, grow counter, last-seen flag or member that survives a Graph step other than pooled node references, the last poll and `diag_latch` (FT-1, FT-41), and no draw, reconcile or selection path reads `diag_latch`. (lint) [FT-1, FT-27, FT-41; PR-8; P1] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-3 Truth tag and read class.** GIVEN every node the system creates, WHEN the scene is walked, THEN each carries the TRUTH_PX grade of the Filter's PerceptionTag (registry: `perception_tag`), and the source reads no `PERCEPTION_OUT` view and calls no `true_value()`. (lint) [FT-2; LS-14; PR-10; P4]
- **AC-4 Bit-identical under the Filter.** GIVEN the Perception Filter at its maximum stage (violet bleed on pipe silhouettes) and a frost fan beside a pipe, WHEN the trail region is captured with the Filter pass on and off, THEN every trail pixel is bit-identical and only the pipe silhouette differs; the capture pair is retained in `production/qa/evidence/` (signing lead: art-director). (auto-render) [FT-2; PR-10, `PIPE:989`; P4] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-5 Filter-disabled path.** GIVEN the Filter's mask unavailable (it disables its own pass, `PIPE:735`), WHEN a frame is rendered, THEN the output equals the frame with the mask available and no code path branches on the Filter's state. (auto-render) [FT-2; PR-10; P4] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-6 No phantom trail (independent oracle).** GIVEN a class (a) phantom entity active at sanity stage 3 and the descriptor feed `fx_row_oracle.json`, WHEN the resolver's trail sources are counted, THEN the count equals the number of oracle rows marked "draws at this sev" in that file, which is **written by hand from the table of record and never generated from the resolver** (rows 6, 10, 22 and 23 never; 21 only at sev 4; 20 only at sev 2 or more; 24 and 25 by their own rules; 27 at sev 1 for every medium but GAS, which draws nothing); a second run at sanity stage 0 gives the identical set; and no node exists whose source descriptor is absent. (auto) [FT-2, FT-3, FT-39; LS-14; P4] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-7 Descriptor-only drawing.** GIVEN a derelict section with no authored fault, WHEN it is instantiated and rendered, THEN zero trail nodes exist; GIVEN one descriptor whose row draws at its `sev`, THEN exactly one trail source exists for it (a source may own several stamp nodes: a chain, a patch set, a puddle set). (auto) [FT-3; LS-14; P1]
- **AC-8 Anchor order.** GIVEN a `2 SHORT` and a `3 OVERHEAT` both with `subject_id` 41 on one anchor, WHEN rendered, THEN two trails draw in ascending (`subject_id`, `mode`, `medium`) order, each with its own stamp (a `2 SHORT` and a `3 OVERHEAT` are POINT rows and have no extent; two RUN descriptors would each have their own extent). (auto) [FT-3; P1] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review)*
- **AC-9 Forbidden elements.** GIVEN the scene and sheets, WHEN scanned, THEN no label, meter, bar, icon, outline, highlight, beacon, arrow or alarm-colour pixel is produced by the system, and nothing is parented to a crewmate or to a machine body sprite. (lint) [FT-4, FT-24; `LSG:1003`; P1]
- **AC-88 Sanity and class sweep.** GIVEN the same Graph state, WHEN the derived render state is dumped (auto) and the trail pixels are captured (auto-render) at sanity stages 0-3, under each hallucination class (a)-(d), and for two co-op players at different stages, THEN all dumps and all captures are identical. (auto, auto-render) [FT-2; knob invariant 8; P4] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-89 Upstream evidence and continuity.** GIVEN a trail on an edge, WHEN drawn at any extent, THEN stamps are contiguous (`start(i+1) = start(i) + STAMP_PX[idx_i]`), the thickest stamp is at the source, and no stamp lies on a node with no upstream evidence on the connecting edge. (auto) [FT-3; D.1; P1]
- **AC-91 No `intensity_pm` computed here.** GIVEN the source, WHEN scanned, THEN it contains no expression that produces an `intensity_pm` value; it only reads the field. (lint) [FT-30]
- **AC-92 Footprint kinds.** GIVEN `deposit_trace` of kind CHILL, BURN and STRESS that change no descriptor, THEN zero nodes are created; GIVEN 17 footprint writes in one step, THEN only the effects of the 16 the Graph accepted (`MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` 16) are drawn; GIVEN a GOUGE on a duct that yields only WORN, THEN nothing draws, and if it yields a LEAK the LEAK row draws. (auto, integration with the Graph) [FT-31]
- **AC-93 Read-only on the Graph.** GIVEN the source, WHEN scanned, THEN it calls only `read_view` queries (`failures`, `compartment`, `node`, `edge`) and no mutator (M1-M18, including M17 `deposit_trace`), and writes no `graph.state` field. (lint) [FT-1; LS-19; CR-9]
- **AC-168 Identity tuple includes `medium`.** GIVEN two `26 SEAL_STRAIN` descriptors on one hatch, one `medium` GAS and one HEAT, with the same `subject_id`, `mode` and anchor, WHEN rendered, THEN two trails exist (bowed rim and rim frost), in ascending `medium` order, and no merge occurs; GIVEN two descriptors identical in all five identity fields, THEN the resolver raises a diagnostic and draws one. (auto) [FT-3] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

### B. Signal contract, size and extent (D.1, D.2, D.4)

- **AC-10 Size table.** GIVEN `sev` 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, WHEN `trail_size` runs, THEN `size_idx` is 0, 1 (trace), 1 (full), 2, 3, and `sev` 0 draws nothing. (auto) [FT-6; D.1; LS-13; P2]
- **AC-11 Seam weep is sev 1 (the exception is retired).** GIVEN `FX-SEAM` (a SEAM descriptor, `1 LEAK/GAS`, sev 1, `A_seam` 1, `intensity_pm` 15, `since_steps` 0 at the weld), WHEN the resolver runs, THEN `size_idx` is 1 with `sub_tier` trace, the state is DRAWN_LIVE, `density_level` 1 and `cover16` 8 (the seam floor, AC-152), the draw row is the mist along the bead; GIVEN the same descriptor at `intensity_pm` 0 (a STILL gas plume) or with `medium` NONE, THEN zero pixels draw (FT-18) and the descriptor still resolves; GIVEN a SEAM descriptor at sev 0, THEN nothing draws and no special case exists in the source (lint: the strings `seam_exception` and `sev_g` are absent). (auto, lint) [FT-6, FT-14; LS-15, `LSG:170`; P1] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-12 Chain taper.** GIVEN `TAPER_STAMPS` 1 and sev 4, WHEN the chain is laid, THEN stamp starts are 0, 144, 240, 288, 336; for sev 3 they are 0, 96, 144, 192; with `TAPER_STAMPS` 2 and sev 4 they are 0, 144, 288, 384, 480, 528; no stamp is larger than the source stamp. (auto) [FT-6; D.1]
- **AC-13 Density levels.** GIVEN `intensity_pm` 0, 1, 299, 300, 599, 600, 899, 900, 1000 and `DENSITY_BUCKETS_PER_LEVEL` 3, WHEN `trail_density` runs, THEN `density_level` is 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4 and `cover16` is 0, 4, 4, 8, 8, 12, 12, 16, 16; no non-zero level draws fewer than `DITHER_MIN_CELLS` 2 cells; GIVEN the seam-weep mist row, THEN `cover16` is 0, 8, 8, 8, 8, 12, 12, 16, 16 (the `COVER16_FLOOR` of 8 binds at levels 1 and 2). (auto) [FT-5; D.4; LS-20] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-14 Accent regardless of flow.** GIVEN a pipe at sev 3 with `intensity_pm` 40, WHEN rendered, THEN the heavy-frost collar (or wet collar, or deep scorch pit) draws at `cover16` 16 while the moving media run at level 1; GIVEN sev 2, THEN no sev 3+ accent draws. (auto) [FT-5; D.4; P1]
- **AC-15 Extent bounds.** GIVEN sev 3, `edge_len_px` 336 (assumed fixture), `T` -2000 mC, WHEN `grow_steps` is 0, 10, 48, 56, THEN `trail_extent_px` is 48, 60, 288, 336; the extent is monotone non-decreasing in `grow_steps` and never exceeds `edge_len_px`. (auto) [FT-8; D.2, D.3; P2] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-16 Tell window at every severity.** GIVEN the `FX-TELL` feed (a 288 base px edge in a room whose `frost_reach` is at least 288 px, `T` -12000 mC, reach 864 px; each descriptor with `grow_steps` 0 on its first frame), WHEN each of sev 1-4 is stepped, THEN it crosses the room in at most 288 steps (28.8 s) at every sev, and in exactly 144, 96, 48 and 20 steps at the placeholder rates (14.4, 9.6, 4.8 and 2.0 s). The sev-1 case is **the seam weep** (`FX-SEAM` on a 288 px edge: GAS, no reach bound, a true onset from `built_step`, so it needs no GA-T) and, as a second sev-1 case, the `4 FREEZE` pre-stage; the sev-2 case is the `5 BREACH` pre-stage hairline, the sev-3 case the `1 LEAK/COOLANT` descriptor and the sev-4 case the `5 BREACH` bent rib. (auto) [FT-9; D.2; `PIPE:1081` item 15; LS-13; P2] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-17 Faster than walking, not faster than running.** GIVEN `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[4]`, WHEN checked against `V_WALK` 2 and `V_RUN` 3 px per tick (12 and 18 px per Graph step), THEN 12 < `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[4]` <= 18. GIVEN a straight 1152 px edge, the source at x = 0, a hull plate whose `sev` rises from 3 to 4 (so `grow_steps` is 0 on the `N/` frame: a state the fairness gate can produce, unlike the former `since_steps` >= 100 start), and a player at x = 144 moving away at 120 px/s (walking), then in a second run at 180 px/s (running), WHEN 10 s elapse, THEN the front `max(48, 15 x n)` reaches the walker at step 48 (720 px, the walker at 144 + 12 x 48) and is ahead from step 49, and never reaches the runner (15 n < 144 + 18 n for every n). (auto) [FT-9; `ART:224`; P2] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-18 Slower than the drip.** GIVEN the cryo-bay fixture (sev 3), WHEN `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[3]` x 10 is compared with `DRIP_FALL_PX_PER_FRAME` x `TRAIL_ANIM_FPS`, THEN 60 <= 72, and the knob lint refuses any tuning that breaks the inequality. (auto) [FT-9; D.2 invariant (iv); `ART:142`]
- **AC-19 Severity change restarts the trail.** GIVEN a hull plate at sev 3 with `mode_steps` 100 crossing to sev 4, WHEN the `N/` key arrives, THEN the next rendered frame shows the l drawing with `grow_steps` 0, extent 48 (`thr` 42 of 127) and no intermediate frame; the extent is 48 at `grow_steps` 3, 60 at 4, 75 at 5 and reaches 288 at `grow_steps` 20; GIVEN sev 4 falling to 3, THEN the same restart applies at 6 px per step. (auto) [FT-8; T6] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-20 Smoothing is optional and bounded.** GIVEN `TRAIL_EXTENT_SMOOTH` true, sev 3, `edge_len_px` 336, `T` -2000 mC, `grow_steps` 48 (so `E(47)` = 282 and `E(48)` = 288), WHEN `alpha_pm` is 0, 500 and 999, THEN `E_disp` is 282, 285 and 287 and never reaches 288 before the next Graph step; GIVEN `TRAIL_EXTENT_SMOOTH` false, THEN `E_disp` = `E(n)`; extrapolation never occurs. (auto) [FT-8; D.2; `KERN:298`] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-21a Cascade extents.** GIVEN a five-hop cascade (one hop per Graph run, at most `MAX_SPREAD_PER_STEP` 32 new failures per run), WHEN each newly failed edge first draws, THEN its extent is 48 at its own `grow_steps` 0. (auto) [FT-10; LS-12; P2] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-21b No front state.** GIVEN the source, WHEN scanned, THEN no hop counter, front position or propagation animation state exists. (lint) [FT-10; FT-1]
- **AC-94 Density table and keys.** GIVEN `intensity_pm` 299 then 300, WHEN the Graph emits its `F/` key, THEN `density_level` changes 1 to 2 exactly in that key's render callback; `DRIP_PER_S` is 2 and `FRAMES_ACTIVE` is 4 at level 2. (auto) [FT-5; D.4; T7]
- **AC-95 Asset manifest.** GIVEN the MVP asset list, WHEN checked, THEN s-frost, s-scorch, s-hairline, s-strain, **s-mist (trace and full), s-puddle and `vfx_o2_mist_drift_s`** exist; no propagation-frame asset exists. (lint) [FT-7; FT-14; FT-21] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-96 Age clamp.** GIVEN `grow_steps` 20000, 65535 and 1,000,000, WHEN `trail_extent` runs, THEN extent equals `edge_len_px`, no integer overflow occurs, `age_px` stops growing at `SINCE_CLAMP` 20000, and `dull_pm` still follows `mode_steps` unclamped. (auto) [FT-8; D.2, D.5] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-97 Short edge and head reveal.** GIVEN `edge_len_px` 24, WHEN drawn, THEN extent is 24, the source stamp is clipped by the reveal threshold with no scaling and no pixel beyond the edge; GIVEN sev 4 at `grow_steps` 0 on a long edge, THEN extent is 48 and `thr` = floor(48 x 127 / 144) = 42 (sev 3: 63); the source is shown, partly, as ruled (F-4). (auto) [FT-8; D.2, D.10] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-98 Long edge and severity fall.** GIVEN `edge_len_px` 1300, THEN the trail draws the full 1300 px, a content lint error is raised and nothing is shortened; GIVEN sev 4 falling to 3 at `mode_steps` 100 on a 336 px edge, THEN the next frame's extent is 48 (the restart, `grow_steps` 0), the size swaps down in one frame, and the extent is `min(336, 6 x grow_steps)` thereafter. (auto, lint) [FT-8; T6] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-99 Growth invariants.** GIVEN the knob table, WHEN linted, THEN `GROW_PX_PER_STEP[1]` >= 1, the array is monotone non-decreasing in `sev`, and sev 4 is in (12, 18]. (lint) [FT-9; knob invariant 1]
- **AC-167 Density-level reachability.** GIVEN `DENSITY_BUCKETS_PER_LEVEL` swept over its legal range 2-3 and `intensity_pm` 0-1000 in steps of 1, WHEN `trail_density` runs, THEN every one of the levels 1, 2, 3 and 4 is reached at both widths (level 4 from 900 at width 3, from 600 at width 2), the sequence is monotone non-decreasing, and the knob lint rejects a width of 4 or 5. (auto, lint) [FT-5; D.4] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-152 Seam mist legibility floor.** GIVEN the seam-weep mist at `A_seam` 1 (`intensity_pm` 15), `A_seam` 5 (78), `A_seam` 20 (312) and `A_seam` 64 (1000), WHEN `cover16` is resolved, THEN it is 8, 8, 8 and 16 (floors and levels 1, 1, 2, 4); and no other row's `cover16` is affected by the floor. (auto) [FT-14; D.4] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-100 Growth tip frame.** GIVEN extents 48, 96, 144 and 336, WHEN `tip_frame` runs, THEN it is 1, 2, 0 and 1 (`floor(extent / 48) mod 3`) and does not change with `present_time`. (auto) [FT-21; D.8]
- **AC-145 Wear then leak is born fresh.** GIVEN a fuel pipe whose `since_steps` is 18000 (it was WORN for 30 minutes) and which crosses `LEAK_HP` this step, entering mode `1 LEAK` with `mode_since_step` = this step, WHEN its first LEAK frame resolves, THEN `grow_steps` 0, `trail_extent_px` 48 (`MIN_EXTENT_PX`), `dull_step` 0, `fuel_dried` false and the Fuel Ember edge draws. (auto) [FT-8, FT-17; D.2, D.5; GA-T] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-146 Isolation freezes the extent.** GIVEN a sev 3 coolant leak on a 336 px edge at `T` -2000 mC, WHEN a closed valve isolates it at `grow_steps` 50 (`isolated_at_step` set), THEN `trail_extent_px` is 300 on that step and still 300 100 steps later (the descriptor is DRAWN_STILL, no drip); GIVEN the same isolation of a `1 LEAK/GAS` descriptor, THEN `trail_extent_px` is likewise frozen at its value and zero pixels draw (FT-18); GIVEN the valve reopened, THEN `grow_steps` rejoins `mode_steps` and the extent steps once to `min(336, 6 x mode_steps)`; GIVEN a `sev` change while isolated, THEN `grow_steps` is 0 and never negative. (auto) [FT-8, FT-17, FT-18; D.2; GA-T] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-147 A severity rise on an aged subject grows from the new onset.** GIVEN a hull plate at sev 3 with `mode_steps` 300 and extent at the edge, WHEN its `sev` rises to 4 and the Graph resets `mode_since_step`, THEN on the `N/` frame `grow_steps` is 0, the size is l, the extent is 48, and 20 steps later it is `min(edge, 300)`; the previous 336 px extent is not carried over. (auto) [FT-8, T6; GA-T] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
- **AC-175 No legacy fallback; the non-dominant interim only.** GIVEN the resolver source, WHEN scanned, THEN the only read of `since_steps` for extent or dullness is the branch for a non-dominant seam weep (`1 LEAK/GAS` on a SEAM); GIVEN a record that lacks `mode_steps` or `grow_steps` (a Graph regression), THEN the resolver draws the head stamp only and writes one diagnostic line per `(log_id, subject_id)` rising edge naming the missing field. (auto, lint) [FT-8, FT-30; GA-T] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the legacy path is deleted, GA-T being adopted)*
- **AC-181 Non-dominant descriptors, tested on the hero seam.** GIVEN `FX-SEAM` (weep sev 1, `since_steps` 144, 288 px edge) with a mode-5 BREACH pre-stage added at sev 1, THEN the weep is dominant (lower mode id) and the BREACH hairline, non-dominant, draws its head only (extent 48, `dull_step` 0); GIVEN the pre-stage rises to sev 2, THEN the BREACH becomes dominant, the Graph restamps its onset, its extent is 48 on that frame and grows at 3 px per step, and the weep, now non-dominant, still draws at its `built_step` age (extent 288: no jump, no shrink); GIVEN a LEAK (sev 3) and a FREEZE (sev 1) on one pipe, THEN the FREEZE sheath draws its head only (48 px, `dull_step` 0) until it becomes dominant; in every case no trail's extent increases by more than 18 px (`GROW_PX_PER_STEP[4]` x 1 step) between two consecutive frames and no trail is undrawn. (auto) [FT-8, FT-19; LS-14; GA-T] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
- **AC-186 BREACH hole variant is keyed on value.** GIVEN a sev-4 `5 BREACH` descriptor with `intensity_pm` 0, 400, 484, 500, 640, 687, 699, 700, 703, 850, 890, 899, 900, 906, 1000 (taken as given from the Graph), THEN 0, 400, 484 draw the bent rib without a hole, 500, 640, 687, 699 draw hole variant 0, 700, 703, 850, 890, 899 variant 1, 900, 906, 1000 variant 2, and no hash call is made for the choice (the injected `hash_fn` call count is unchanged); GIVEN the same plate at sev 4 with and without a hole, THEN the two resolve to different stamps; the resolver derives no `A_hole` (AC-91). (auto) [row 5, D.6; FT-30 item 7] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6, inputs recomputed from the Graph formula)*

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

content.content:
# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

1352	## Acceptance Criteria
1353	
1354	*Format: GIVEN / WHEN / THEN, one or more per core rule and per formula, then cross-system and budget criteria. Tags: **(auto)** an automated unit or integration test on the pure resolver (FT-39) or the poll logic that runs **headless** in the mandated CI command (`tests/unit/failure_and_trail/`, `tests/integration/failure_and_trail/`), BLOCKING; **(auto-render)** an automated test that needs rendered pixels (captures, bit-identity, dither, containment) and runs on the named render job `ft-render` (FT-40), never on the headless job, BLOCKING; **(lint)** a static or build-time scan, BLOCKING; **(manual)** a retained capture in `production/qa/evidence/` with sign-off by the named lead, BLOCKING (Visual/Feel and UI evidence is not waived at `qa.level: minimal`); **(spike)** needs a measured spike, named by id, with its pass threshold stated, before the story can close. Fixtures are the data files of `tests/fixtures/failure_and_trail/` (FT-40: `FX-CRYO`, `FX-SEAM`, `FX-TELL`, `fx_row_oracle.json` and the three budget fixtures). Performance criteria are gated on the two reference machines of `project.yaml` `qa.min_spec` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*: **RM-DESKTOP** (Windows 10/11 64-bit; 6-core / 6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class; 8 GB RAM; GPU of the GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / Radeon RX 570 4 GB class, Vulkan 1.2+; SATA SSD; 1920x1080 at 60 Hz; P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 16.6 ms) and **RM-DECK** (Steam Deck LCD 2022, SteamOS stable, 1280x800 at 60 Hz, 30 fps target, ceiling 33.3 ms). Every wall-clock figure is a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release export template, not the editor and not a debug template), renderer `forward_plus`, vsync on, 120 warm-up frames, with the startup read-back (renderer, driver) recorded; a frame-level pass needs P99 <= 90 % of the ceiling (headroom >= 1.7 ms desktop, >= 3.3 ms Deck); the developer's machine is indicative only. A criterion that names RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK passes only when it passes on each; a value not yet measured is "pending spike measurement on RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK", not blocked. **Measurement protocol for every frame-time criterion** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the criterion states its sample (at least 600 Graph steps, about 3,600 render frames, of a scripted player walking at `V_WALK`, and at least 100 samples in every frame class it judges), its percentile method (nearest-rank p99 over the samples of that class) and writes a **host header** into its evidence file (CPU, GPU, OS, driver, display mode and whether the run was an editor or an exported run, as recorded by the harness). The header records what ran and is checked against the named machines and build above. **Reviewer pool RP-3 (defined once, cited by every reviewing criterion):** three reviewers, none of whom authored the capture and none of whom has seen its label: the art-director, the qa-lead and one participant from outside the team (a PT-1 participant); each classifies independently and in writing before any discussion; unless a criterion states another threshold, a classification passes when all three are correct for m and l at `k_auto` and the first zoom-out, and at least two of three are correct for s-tier captures and for k = 1. Citation form `[FT-n; LS-n; PR-n; CR-n; SL-n; EM-n; pillar]`: `LS-` the Life-Support Graph, `PR-` the Pipeline, `CR-` the kernel, `SL-` Save/Load, `EM-` Emitter State; `D.n` a formula of this GDD. Captures are taken **lit** (the chest lamp's beam on the trail) unless a criterion says dark. Every number is a registry constant, a Graph value cited by name, a worked value from this GDD's formulas, or a **[PLACEHOLDER]** default; every pass or fail value is stated in the criterion, never only behind a citation. Criteria that need the GA-T fields (`mode_steps`, `grow_steps`) set them in the fixture feed, so they run now against the resolver; the Graph-side half of GA-T is checked by the Graph's own criteria. Criterion ids are stable handles in one sequence (AC-1 to AC-188, with lettered splits); groups are by topic, so ids within a group are not contiguous. Criteria that wait on a neighbour that does not exist yet (the VS-B MIRROR path), and the points that are not testable as written, are in **Gaps / untestable as written** at the end. # Design Document Rules

I'm weighing whether AC-35's cost model, with its injectable cost source instead of wall clock, deserves its own entry beyond what TR-009 already covers for budget logging thresholds.

I'm also checking several other candidates against existing coverage: AC-186c's load-time refusal of constant desync looks new, while AC-175/AC-110/AC-111's degraded-input contracts suggest a build-time lint requiring every Graph descriptor id to have a table-of-record row, which I want to include as a cross-system contract. AC-180's seeded onset survival and fixture loader rejection rules point to a Graph-side GA-T triple and phase-9 preservation contract worth including, while AC-103's integer bounds are already covered by TR-011, and I'm now looking at AC-134's rng_derive mapping against TR-022.

Going through the rest, AC-150's deterministic patch order seems narrow enough to skip, AC-92's footprint is Graph-only, and AC-33's dormant behavior is already covered by AC-180. AC-34's pause requirement — that present_time freezes when paused — seems worth including as a threading/timing cross-system item, while AC-142, AC-32, and AC-31 all look already covered by TR-007, TR-001, and TR-009 respectively.

content.thinking:
I'm looking at AC-60/61 around the glow table and the FAULT_GLOW record requirement, with the MAX_FAULT_GLOW cap of 10 belonging to Emitter's territory. TR-018 already covers the glow table, but AC-61's timing constraint—requiring exactly one FAULT_GLOW record on the Graph tick and never later—suggests a cross-system hook ordering issue where Emitter needs to derive FAULT_GLOW from descriptors on that same tick.

Checking AC-64's flash clamp and the regional swing computation for compartment-crossing arcs, I think this is only partially covered by TR-028 and should be skipped given it's narrower than needed. AC-135's knob lint for rejecting invalid values rather than clamping seems foldable into a single Data row combining AC-135, AC-186c, AC-99, and AC-18 around boot-time lint refusal tied to TR-006 and TR-012. AC-58's dark room and AC-124's distortion shader both look covered by TR-018 and TR-016 respectively, though AC-127 on materials needs more thought.

I'm noting that no material should read the screen texture or displace UVs, folding this into Rendering alongside the TR-003 bit-identity constraint. AC-132's resize behavior is covered by TR-008/010, and AC-47's degradation ordering is sufficiently addressed by TR-019. AC-140's cross-system exposure contract falls under TR-018, while AC-63a and AC-108 are already covered by TR-028/TR-001.
